name: Rosewood Amsterdam
positioning: Luxury hotel in Amsterdam's former Palace of Justice on Prinsengracht, in the Canal District, with interiors by Studio Piet Boon
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable Canal District base in a historic building
Groups or families wanting a House with a kitchen and dedicated butler, or connected suites

facts.text: Rosewood Amsterdam occupies a historic spot in the heart of Amsterdam's Canal District.
The hotel is set on Prinsengracht, one of Amsterdam's four main canals.
The building was built in the 17th century as an orphanage.
The interiors were designed by Amsterdam-based Studio Piet Boon.
Rooms are decorated in a palette of rich grays and deep blues with layered textures and curated art.
The Houses have full kitchens, sweeping lounges and walk-in wardrobes.
Connected suites let families stay together.
Eeuwen's menu celebrates seasonal produce from farms in the Netherlands and its neighbors.
The Court is an all-day venue serving from morning coffee and Tompouce to pre-dinner drinks.
Asaya Spa draws on traditional Eastern healing practices and Ayurvedic traditions.
There is a 24-hour gym, group classes and steam rooms.
The hotel offers a salon boat tour of Amsterdam aboard the boat Liberty with Dutch treats.

highlights.text: The building is the former Palace of Justice of Amsterdam.
The building's former holding cells have been turned into a feature of the hotel.
Advocatuur is the hotel's bar and distillery, with mixology centered on its own home-distilled jenever.
Guests can take a guided genever tasting in the former cells.
The hotel holds a collection of around 1,000 artworks.

considerations.text: The spa has a small swimming pool.
Most of the city can be reached on foot from the hotel, and the hotel has bikes for guests.

sources.title: Rosewood Amsterdam review - Condé Nast Traveler
